newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African rand tumbles to record lows.
newsitem.headline: S.African rand tumbles to record lows.

text.p: The South African rand lost a further 2-1/2 cents against the dollar on Thursday morning, tumbling through 4.75 to trade at an all-time low of 4.7670/7720.
Against the British pound it fell to 7.7782/7887 from 7.7185/73148 on Wednesday.

Dealers said the main factor driving the market on Thursday was importers selling rand for dollars but that the currency was also vulnerable to further speculative attacks, with many analysts expecting a test of the 4.80 level in the short-term.

The rand has lost over 30 percent against the dollar since February, battered by speculators who see it as a one-way bet given South Africa's low reserves, balance of payments problems and its pledge to scrap exchange controls some time in the future.

South Africa's two business newspapers on Thursday called on the government to bite the bullet and scrap exchange controls immediately, backed up by support from the International Monetary Fund, to end the agony in the foreign exchange markets.

"(Finance Minister Trevor) Manuel and (Reserve Bank Governor Chris) Stals cannot delay the complete removal of exchange controls if further damage to the currency and the economy are to be avoided," Business Day said in an editorial.
Business Report said the possible one-off fall in the rand with the scrapping of controls was preferable to continued speculative attacks.
"Obviously, lifting exchange controls would stop the rot by collapsing the rand to a real floor. Surely that has to be preferable to the drip-drip of water torture by speculation."
So far, however, the authorities have rejected such a radical move.
Stals has said on several occasions in recent days that calls for the immediate scrapping of controls were unreasonable while reserves remain precariously low.
Manuel told parliament on Wednesday that the only proper response to the falling value of the rand lay in the steady implementation of the government's announced macro-economic strategy.
